title: Admin Pulselet: Curated lightweight runbook tasks and autopilot index
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a curated catalog of small, composable admin tasks ("pulselets") that can be executed as first-class runbook tasks. Goal is to reduce MTTR for common ops actions by providing audited, parameterized, and safety-gated micro-runbooks backed by the runbook executor. This ticket covers schema, storage, discovery, simple UI surfacing in the Ops Console, and an autopilot index that recommends pulselets during incident triage.
acceptance_criteria: Pulselet registry schema defined and documented in Confluence
Backend storage implemented (S3 + manifest) and integrated with existing runbook executor API
At least 20 seeded pulselets for common tasks (rotate-key, service-restart, cache-evict, rollout-fallback)
Ops Console can search and preview pulselets with human-readable descriptions and risk level
Execution of a pulselet produces structured provenance (who/when/params) and emits telemetry to admin-telemetry pipeline
Safety gating: pulselets with high risk require RBAC approval and opt-in audit logging
Autopilot index suggests top-3 pulselets during triage based on alert fingerprints and recent run history
decisions: Use a lightweight manifest (YAML) stored in curated S3 bucket instead of a new DB to keep discovery fast and portable
Pulselets are parameterized templates executed by the existing runbook executor (no separate runtime) to avoid doubling maintenance
Implement risk levels (low/medium/high) and map high-risk pulselets to a two-step approval flow in Console
Autopilot index will be a simple scoring service (TF-IDF of alert tags + recent success rates) for MVP; defer ML modelization to follow-up
notes: This is intentionally different from previous "runbook-as-playlet" efforts by focusing on ultra-small composable tasks (3-10 lines) that non-privileged responders can use
Trade-off: S3 manifest reduces transactional consistency vs DB but simplifies rollbacks and cross-environment portability
We must ensure no pulselet embeds long-lived secrets. Parameter validation and per-exec KMS envelope will be enforced
We should coordinate with Security for the RBAC mapping and with SRE for initial pulselet catalog curation
